text: You're at the coffee shop, needing that perfect drink. You just want your order to be fast, correct, and get you moving.
But before your coffee, the barista asks for your name. You give it, they scribble it onto your cup, a familiar ritual.
Why bother? Is it just to prevent mix-ups, a simple efficiency hack? Or perhaps old-fashioned politeness?
The truth: writing your name creates a tiny, personal connection. It makes you feel seen, unique, part of their world, not just another customer.
This small gesture taps into your desire for recognition. It builds subconscious loyalty, making you feel more welcome than at a faceless competitor.
So next time your name is called, remember: it's not just about the coffee. It's an invisible system designed to bring you back.
